objectives: To learn the principles and techniques of dimensioning and preparing engineering drawings.
To develop the ability to accurately interpret and understand engineering drawings.
To learn the features of CAD software

modules.title: Introduction & Projection of Points and Lines

topics.title: Introduction
subtopics: Relevance of technical drawing in engineering field
Types of lines
Dimensioning
BIS code of practice for technical drawing. (No questions for the end semester examination)

topics.title: Projection of points and lines
subtopics: Projection of points in different quadrants
Projection of straight lines inclined to one plane and inclined to both planes
Trace of a line
Inclination of lines with reference planes
True length and true inclinations of line inclined to both the reference planes

topics.title: Projection of Simple solids
subtopics: Projection of Simple solids such as Triangular, Rectangle, Square, Pentagonal and Hexagonal Prisms, Pyramids, Cone and Cylinder only
Projection of solids in simple position including profile view
Projection of solids with axis inclined to one of the reference planes and with axis inclined to both reference planes

modules.title: Sections of Solids & Development of Surfaces

topics.title: Sections of Solids
subtopics: Sections of Prisms, Pyramids, Cone and Cylinder only, with axis in vertical position and cut by different section planes
True shape of the sections. (Exclude true shape given problems)

topics.title: Development of Surfaces
subtopics: Development of surfaces of the solids and solids cut by different section planes. (Exclude problems with through holes)

topics.title: Isometric Projection
subtopics: Isometric scale
Isometric View and Projections of Prisms, Pyramids, Cone, Cylinder, Sphere, Hemisphere and their combinations

topics.title: Computer Aided Drawing (CAD)
subtopics: Introduction
Role of CAD in design and development of new products
Advantages of CAD
Creating two-dimensional drawing with dimensions using suitable software. (CAD, only internal evaluation)

outcomes: Understand the projection of points and lines located in different quadrants
Prepare multiview orthographic projections of objects by visualizing them in different positions
Plot sectional views and develop surfaces of a given object
Prepare pictorial drawings using the principles of isometric projection
Sketch simple drawing using CAD tools.
ese: The examination has 8 questions, two from each module; answer one full question from each module.
Each answered question carries 15 marks. Total: 4 × 15 = 60 marks. There is no Part A/Part B split.
